qa_stack.profile: there is no stack to bring up and no port to reach. The product is reached over a process boundary: a check runs `python3 -m tally` through the opted-in `python3` tool and reads the exit code, the two streams, and the files the command left behind. The target's driver is `python`, which names the harness the scenario body runs in rather than the transport to the product — there is no separate driver for a command. `qa.tool` runs at the repo root and cannot be given a working directory, so a scenario names its own ledger with `--file` under the evidence directory rather than sharing `tally.json` with every other scenario
fixtures: a directory the scenario owns under the evidence dir, named on every invocation with `--file`, so two scenarios never write the same ledger
nothing installed and nothing resolved: `python3 -m tally` runs the package out of the repo root, which is where `qa.tool` already runs
qa_stack.capable_of_rendering: nothing. `tally` opens no port and renders nothing; the observables are an exit code, stdout, stderr, and the files left on disk
qa_stack.notes: the one tool this lane opts into is `python3`, declared in `agents.yml` under `qa: {tools: [python3]}` and defined in the tracked table at `paddock/data/configs/`. It is the interpreter, not the app: a plan may not import the package it tests, because `ostler.qa.lint` is an AST allowlist, so being written in the harness's own language buys `tally` no shortcut to being reached
